```{r setup, include=FALSE}
figure_dir <- params$figure_dir
if(is.null(figure_dir)) {figure_dir <- tempfile("traffic-figures-");dir.create(figure_dir)}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=TRUE,
  fig.path=file.path(figure_dir,"figure-"), dev="png", dpi=150,
  fig.width=10, fig.height=8, out.width="100%", cache=FALSE)
fmt <- function(v,digits=2) format(round(v,digits),trim=TRUE,scientific=FALSE,big.mark=",")
stopifnot(is.logical(params$export),length(params$export)==1L,!is.na(params$export))
```

## Sources and measurements

The example contains 24 hourly frames on 2026-06-16. Los Angeles Area uses D07, D08 and D12 records; San Francisco Bay Area uses D04 records. Flow and CHP starts are shown separately for each region.

Los Angeles hourly station values come from `flow_2026_06.binz`. D04 uses `d04_text_station_5min_2026_06_16.txt.gz`: twelve complete five-minute counts form each station-hour total. Display-link flow is the mean of available endpoint station values, in vehicles/hour.

The selected records contain 1,019 CHP starts: 700 in Los Angeles and 319 in D04. Each marker represents a reported start in the selected hour. End times are unavailable, so the markers do not establish event duration or an effect on traffic.

## Data preparation

`prepare.R` aligns source stations with the supplied links, forms hourly values and assigns CHP starts to their reported hour and region. The bundled `data/source.rds` records become the common road-flow and event fields in `data/input.rds`.

```{r prepare}
library(bdynets)
source("prepare.R")
prepared_file <- prepare_example(".")
x <- read_traffic(prepared_file)
input <- readRDS(prepared_file)
x$basemap <- traffic_basemap(x,cache_dir=file.path("data","basemap-cache"))
x$provenance$basemap <- x$basemap$provenance
runtime_context <- x$basemap
index <- match(params$time_label,sub("^.* ","",x$time_labels))
stopifnot(!is.na(index))
```

The map starts at `r x$time_labels[index]` and covers
`r x$interval_seconds[index]/60` minutes. The default 08:00 is a demonstration
selection, not a maximum-based selection. Numeric seconds and displayed labels
retain the supplied source clock; they do not establish a UTC offset.

```{r scope}
knitr::kable(data.frame(Region=x$regions,
  Roads=vapply(x$regions,function(z)sum(x$roads$region==z),integer(1)),
  Whole_day_starts=vapply(x$regions,function(z)sum(x$events$region==z),integer(1))),
  caption="Whole-day regional scope")
knitr::kable(head(input$flow),caption="Actual prepared road-hour records")
knitr::kable(head(input$events[c("id","time_label","lon","lat","category","region")]),
  caption="Actual prepared event records")
```

| Common field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| road_id, geometry | Unique display link and travel-ordered longitude/latitude vertices |
| from_station, to_station | Endpoint source station identifiers |
| time, flow | Source-clock hour start and endpoint-mean hourly rate |
| id, time, lon, lat | Unique report ID, reported start and coordinates |
| category, description | Source-type classification and retained source text |
| region | Explicit geographic selection label |

Both regions use the same object, plot method and global log1p thresholds.
Their central-area views do not restrict regional statistics. Red diamonds mark
starts in the selected hour. Geographic overlap alone does not establish a
relationship between a report and a road measurement.

## Los Angeles Area

```{r la-map, fig.cap="Los Angeles Area: road flow and CHP reported starts in the selected hour. Colors use the same full-day, two-region thresholds."}
region <- "Los Angeles Area"
plot(x,index=index,region=region)
```

```{r la-statistics}
coverage <- traffic_coverage(x,region=region)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Statistic=c("Roads","Road-hour cells","Observed cells","Missing cells","Zero cells","Whole-day starts"),
  Value=unlist(coverage[c("roads","road_time_cells","observed","missing","zero","event_starts")],use.names=FALSE)),
  caption="Whole-day coverage")
selected <- traffic_summary(x,index=index,region=region)
knitr::kable(selected[c("time","available","missing","zero","events")],
  caption="Selected-hour observations and starts")
knitr::kable(selected[c("minimum","median","mean","p95","maximum")],
  digits=2,caption="Selected-hour distribution [vehicles/hour]")
```

At `r selected$time`, mean available-link flow is `r fmt(selected$mean)`
vehicles/hour, with `r selected$events` reported starts in this hour.
The whole-day total is `r coverage$event_starts` starts. These statistics have different
time scopes. The 56 unavailable links in each hour produce 1,344 missing road-hour cells. The hourly export does not establish complete five-minute coverage for every underlying Los Angeles station.

```{r la-flow-trend, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Regional mean available-link flow by hour. The dashed line marks the selected map hour."}
trend <- traffic_trend(x,region=region,method="mean")
plot(trend,metric="mean",index=index)
flow_peak <- which.max(trend$mean)
```

The greatest regional mean is `r fmt(trend$mean[flow_peak])` vehicles/hour at
`r trend$label[flow_peak]`. Missing link values are excluded from the mean.
This curve does not measure speed or regional vehicle totals.

```{r la-event-trend, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Reported event starts per source-clock hour. The dashed line marks the selected map hour; durations are not inferred."}
plot(trend,metric="events",index=index)
event_peak <- which.max(trend$events)
```

The largest hourly count is `r trend$events[event_peak]` starts at
`r trend$label[event_peak]`. A coincident change in flow would not by itself
establish an event effect.

## San Francisco Bay Area

```{r bay-map, fig.cap="San Francisco Bay Area: road flow and CHP reported starts in the selected hour. Colors use the same full-day, two-region thresholds."}
region <- "San Francisco Bay Area"
plot(x,index=index,region=region)
```

```{r bay-statistics}
coverage <- traffic_coverage(x,region=region)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Statistic=c("Roads","Road-hour cells","Observed cells","Missing cells","Zero cells","Whole-day starts"),
  Value=unlist(coverage[c("roads","road_time_cells","observed","missing","zero","event_starts")],use.names=FALSE)),
  caption="Whole-day coverage")
selected <- traffic_summary(x,index=index,region=region)
knitr::kable(selected[c("time","available","missing","zero","events")],
  caption="Selected-hour observations and starts")
knitr::kable(selected[c("minimum","median","mean","p95","maximum")],
  digits=2,caption="Selected-hour distribution [vehicles/hour]")
```

At `r selected$time`, mean available-link flow is `r fmt(selected$mean)`
vehicles/hour, with `r selected$events` reported starts in this hour.
The whole-day total is `r coverage$event_starts` starts. These statistics have different
time scopes. All 52,872 D04 road-hour values are present. The source has 2,291 mainline stations; 400665, 406767 and 418817 lack matched geometry and are excluded. The 2,288 retained stations have complete five-minute timestamps. Detector imputation may still be present. Six event summaries lack detail messages and remain included.

```{r bay-flow-trend, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Regional mean available-link flow by hour. The dashed line marks the selected map hour."}
trend <- traffic_trend(x,region=region,method="mean")
plot(trend,metric="mean",index=index)
flow_peak <- which.max(trend$mean)
```

The greatest regional mean is `r fmt(trend$mean[flow_peak])` vehicles/hour at
`r trend$label[flow_peak]`. Missing link values are excluded from the mean.
This curve does not measure speed or regional vehicle totals.

```{r bay-event-trend, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Reported event starts per source-clock hour. The dashed line marks the selected map hour; durations are not inferred."}
plot(trend,metric="events",index=index)
event_peak <- which.max(trend$events)
```

The largest hourly count is `r trend$events[event_peak]` starts at
`r trend$label[event_peak]`. A coincident change in flow would not by itself
establish an event effect.

## Figure and data export

`traffic_export()` writes maps, trend figures and the selected data and summary tables for the same input and interval.

```{r export}
if(params$export) {
  label <- gsub("[^[:alnum:]_-]+","-",x$time_labels[index])
  for(region in x$regions) {
    name <- gsub(" ","-",tolower(region))
    traffic_export(x,file.path(params$export_dir,paste(name,label,sep="-")),
      index=index,region=region,
      input_files=c(source="data/source.rds",prepared="data/input.rds"))
  }
}
```
